pdd.problem: The pathology museum keeps its specimens in old open shelving, so students cannot study them properly and some specimens are deteriorating.
pdd.opportunity: Proper cases would let every second and third year student use the museum for self-study between practical sessions.
pdd.proposed_solution: Install sealed glass display cases and wall cases with lighting, then relabel and remount the collection.
pdd.objectives: Display the full specimen collection in sealed cases before the spring term and open the museum for self-study four days a week.
pdd.success_criteria: All 180 specimens displayed in sealed cases; museum open 4 days a week; student feedback score of at least 4 out of 5.
pdd.stakeholders: Pathology department, second and third year students, facilities office.
pdd.related_target: Teaching & Learning Excellence: better practical teaching spaces.
pdd.description: Display cases and lighting for the pathology museum.

risks.risk: Specimens may be damaged while being moved

past_project_updates.body: Two of the seminar room display screens are still not installed. What is holding them, and when will they be in use?
The vendor replaced the faulty mounting kits on both screens last week. Installation is booked for 20 October, and the department has agreed to sign the handover the same day.

past_pm_messages.body: Please send the delivery note for the exhaust fans when it arrives.

comments.body: The schedule shows the study pods past their baseline date. Please confirm the customs date and what is on site now.

Group study furniture, lockers, book stacks and lending stations are on site (4 of 8 items). The study pods cleared shipping on 9 October; customs clearance is now expected by 30 November, 20 days after the baseline. Installation is re-planned so handover on 29 December still holds.
Lighting, power and data works are about 40% done. The contractor adds a second shift from Monday.
PKR 3.5M was released at MT review for the vendor's site survey and the power-line design, which the MT asked for before sanction. No equipment is ordered until approval.
Planned finish (5 October) has passed. The supplier has confirmed the last panels for 24 October; a project manager is being assigned to close the works.
Scope change noted: the cut-over found ten more closets that need access switches. Costing requested to see whether the installation line can absorb it.
Site visit: lighting panels delivered on 1 October. The structural check is booked for 8 October, before the chillers go up.
Site visit: three of the four lighting bars are fitted. The last one is booked for the night of 18 October.
Site visit: tiling is finished on all floors; fixtures go in this week. On track for 31 October.
Lab stools delivered. The microscopes arrive in two batches, the first on 26 October.

value.heading: About the Project Management Office
value.body:
The Project Management Office (PMO) runs the University's capital programme: every CAPEX project from the first proposal to the handover. We review project documents, track approvals through Finance and senior management, follow progress, risks and money released on each site, and report the portfolio to the Board every month. Each project has a named project manager on its campus, and the PMO is the single point of contact for the whole portfolio.

This is a simulation: every project, figure, document, date and message in it is invented.
